newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa ready for new talks with union.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa ready for new talks with union.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG said on Thursday it was ready to hold further wage talks with the DAG white collar workers trade union, with a new focus on possible job protection measures for employees.

"The company is indicating to the DAG that in this area there is room for further talks," Lufthansa said in a statement. It added that would be asking DAG to give it possible dates for the restart of talks.
DAG was not immediately available for comment.
The offer follows the break-down of negotiations between the two last month on a failure to come to an agreement on DAG's demand for a four percent increase in wages.
Lufthansa had earlier on Thursday said it would be issuing an offer to its employees represented by DAG in a bid to avert what it saw as possible industrial action by them.

The airline said in its later statement that in the light of its offer for new talks it would have "no understanding" for threats of industrial action by the union. DAG for its part has not said whether it plans industrial action.

Lufthansa, which last month struck a two-year pay deal with 50,000 workers represented by the OeTV public sector and transport union, said it would in any case be able to cope with industrial action if it took place.
DAG, which is seeking a four percent rise in wages for its members next year, has said that Lufthansa offers up till now would leave them with a pay rise below inflation.
